title: Volvo will use Nvidia’s tech for hands-free, point-to-point driving
key_facts: Volvo said on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 it plans hands-free, point-to-point driving by 2030, built on Nvidia's autonomous driving stack.
Volvo calls it a Level 2++ system: it handles traffic lights, stop signs and unprotected left turns, but the driver still has to watch the road.
It will use Nvidia's Hyperion platform (chips plus sensors) and Alpamayo software, which uses reasoning models to plan steering, braking and acceleration.
The setup will not include lidar, though Volvo could add it later.
Volvo has not said which models come first; Alwin Bakkenes, head of global software engineering at Volvo Cars, only confirmed launch 'before the end of the decade'.
Volvo had to sideline its Ride Pilot Level 3 system in the US after failing to win regulatory approval, and a lidar plan fell away when supplier Luminar went bankrupt.
quote_evidence: Volvo plans to launch hands-free, point-to-point driving by 2030, powered by Nvidia's latest AI technology.
The setup will not include lidar, though it could include the laser sensor if Volvo decides to add it in the future.
The timeline was also a little vague, with Bakkenes only confirming that it will launch “before the end of the decade.”
why_it_matters_hint: It would bring Tesla-style door-to-door assisted driving to a brand known for safety, but the date and models are vague.
